item.title: Recursive Self-Improvement Framework Boosts Long-Horizon Role-Playing Dialogue Quality
item.description:
Recursive Self-Improvement Framework Boosts Long-Horizon Role-Playing Dialogue Quality

A new paper submitted on 5 Nov 2026 introduces a bounded recursive self‑improvement (RSI) framework aimed at improving long‑horizon role‑playing dialogue.

🔍 Overview

  • Long‑horizon role‑playing dialogue requires consistent character identity, reliable memory, and context‑sensitive interaction.

🧩 How it works

  • The RSI framework revises three components:
    • Original‑character memory
    • Stable persona instructions
    • A policy for constructing turn‑level prompts
  • Repair outcomes are used to update:
    • Diagnostic rules
    • Edit routing
    • Candidate selection
  • The updater is defined as a versioned policy with:
    • Explicit inputs
    • Editable fields
    • Acceptance gates
    • Stopping conditions

📊 Evaluation

  • Evaluation covered:
    • 50 original characters
    • 5 models
    • Two 100‑round conversations per character‑model pair (500 conversations per condition)
  • Bad‑response rate:
    • Before RSI: 14.00 % (6,973 / 49,824)
    • After RSI: 4.94 % (2,459 / 49,793)
    • Reduction: 9.06 percentage points, 64.71 % relative decrease
  • Human evaluation:
    • 600 blinded comparisons
    • RSI wins: 294
    • Ties: 187
    • Losses: 119
    • Win rate among decisive judgments: 71.19 %

💡 Why it matters

  • The results show a measurable improvement in aggregate dialogue quality on the internal test distribution.
  • By addressing memory consistency and persona stability, the framework advances more reliable long‑term interactive agents.

#AI #DialogueSystems #RecursiveImprovement

Source: Recursive Self-Improvement for Long-Horizon Role-Playing Dialogue

item.title: ProcessPrefBench Shows Dialogue History Boosts Preference Alignment but Increases Fabricated Evidence
item.description:
ProcessPrefBench Shows Dialogue History Boosts Preference Alignment but Increases Fabricated Evidence

🔍 Overview

In natural human‑AI dialogue, users’ corrections, requests, and self‑descriptions provide reusable signals about how they want work to be done. ProcessPrefBench investigates whether a preference revealed in one dialogue can influence an assistant’s later answer when the task does not restate it.

🧩 How it works

  • The benchmark draws on three months of natural dialogues from two knowledge workers.
  • It constructs 66 source‑target cases that are separately judged for source evidence and target applicability.
  • Sources are preselected, so the test focuses on application rather than retrieval.
  • Three model configurations are evaluated:
    1. Target‑only prompting
    2. Full‑history prompting
    3. Distilled‑preference (imperative) prompting
  • Answers are scored with a 0‑2 rubric for preference realization, and a task gate flags severe failures.

📊 Results

  • Compared with target‑only prompting, preference realization rises by:
    • 0.204 points with full‑history prompting
    • 0.244 points with distilled‑preference prompting
  • No reliable advantage is observed from the distillation step itself.
  • Fabricated‑evidence failures increase:
    • From 5.8 % under target‑only prompting
    • To 10.1 % under full‑history prompting
    • To 10.4 % under distilled‑preference prompting

⚖️ Implications

ProcessPrefBench highlights a tension in learning from dialogue: leveraging prior interactions can improve preference realization, yet it can also invite fabricated evidence. The authors hope the benchmark will help build assistants that honor a user’s process preferences without sacrificing factual reliability.

#AIAlignment #DialogueSystems #Benchmark #ProcessPreferences

Source: ProcessPrefBench: Evaluating Cross-Task Transfer of Individual Process Preferences from Naturalistic Human-AI Interaction

item.title: ProMediConv Benchmarking Framework and Dataset for Mediation Dialogues
item.description:
ProMediConv Benchmarking Framework and Dataset for Mediation Dialogues

A new benchmarking framework called ProMediConv has been introduced to evaluate mediation‑oriented dialogue models.

🔍 Overview

  • ProMediConv models mediation as a proactive, multi‑stage, party‑aware dialogue process.
  • It incorporates 11 mediation strategies and four party‑behavior (BP) states.

🧩 How it works

  • The framework treats each conversation as a sequence of stages where parties can adopt different behavior patterns.
  • Utterance‑level annotations capture both the strategy employed and the current BP state.

⚙️ Key details

  • Dataset: 972 complete real‑world mediation cases with strategy and BP annotations.
  • Metric: MAD (Mean Attribute Difference) measures BP shifts across the dialogue.
  • Baseline: ProMediAgent is the tailored baseline evaluated alongside diverse models.
Component Description
ProMediConv Benchmarking framework that models mediation as proactive, multi‑stage, party‑aware dialogue, incorporating 11 strategies and four BP states
MAD (Mean Attribute Difference) Fine‑grained metric that captures party‑behavior shifts throughout the dialogue
ProMediAgent Tailored baseline evaluated in the comprehensive benchmark

🚀 Availability

  • The dataset and codebase are accessible at this https URL.

#MediationAI #Benchmarking #DialogueSystems #Dataset

Source: ProMediConv: Benchmarking Proactive Conversational Agents in Legal Dispute Mediation
